content.comment_body: Hello everyone! Is it possible to have two separate PCs (each with a unique IP address) running [product_name] Runtime Advanced [version_no] and both connected simultaneously to the same [product_name] [article_no] (using local TSAP: 02)? When I attempt this, each PC alternates in disconnecting from the PLC every 2-3 seconds. I believe the TSAP setting for each [product_name] Runtime connection needs to be adjusted, but I cannot find this option in the [product_name] engineering tool [version_no] connection settings. For reference, I currently have three other devices connected at the same time to this PLC (a Python3 script using the Snap7 library [local TSAP: 03], an Ignition SCADA [version_no] [local TSAP: n/a], and a Kepware server [local TSAP: 04]). Therefore, it’s confirmed that various devices can read data simultaneously from the [product_name] PLC without issue.
This seems to be a situation best addressed by [company_name] technical support. Consider submitting a support request.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is experiencing regular connection interruptions when trying to run two instances of [product_name] Runtime Advanced simultaneously with a single [product_name] PLC. Other third-party applications are able to access the PLC concurrently without issue, indicating a potential configuration restriction or limitation with the [company_name] software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that multiple instances of [product_name] Runtime Advanced should be able to connect and operate with a single [product_name] PLC at the same time, with no disconnection problems, similar to what is possible for third-party clients.
